hook: A huge black dog kept inside a carefully built imitation of a crossroads. The rule is simple, eye contact, but the consequence plays out over a full year and may fall on a family member instead of the person who looked. Read the containment procedures as closely as the description; they hold much of the story.
whyItMatters: This Series I entry takes familiar folklore imagery, a black dog, a crossroads, burning eyes, and turns it into architecture, complete with false doors and eye inserts. Its delayed, partly random consequence gives it a slow, domestic kind of dread rather than an instant one. Addendum 023-004 explicitly ties it to SCP-1111-1, linking the two files.
thingsToNotice: The containment layout is the narrative: a walled-off intersection of two corridors, three fake doors, rubber inserts swapped one at a time and only after sunset, and a ban on reflective surfaces added after a later incident. Each rule implies an earlier failure that the file only partly explains. The observation about family size and the observer's own risk is a small, cold detail that changes how you picture every exposure.

related.note: Addendum 023-004 names SCP-1111-1 as a possible variant of the same phenomenon.
